method.metric: host elapsed time from trusted browser click-command start to the same content marker entering the target DOM

cases.github: First repository directory link inside main
cases.bilibili: Fourth video-title link under main h3

method.cache: Previously visited sites; one additional Firefox warmup per site is excluded. In-app browser sites had already been visited repeatedly. HTTP/DNS/CDN caches are not controlled or forcibly disabled.
method.controls: Same host and URLs, default graphics/cache/security/process preferences, separate Firefox test profile, visible Trames window, no sampler/build/syscall profiler or verbose HTTP log during retained timing runs.
timing_limits: In-app browser Performance/Navigation Timing globals are not exposed by the available API; no in-page FCP/TTI comparison is claimed.
DOM attachment is not screen-present time, complete subresource loading, video-start latency or proof that every control is responsive.
Firefox uses Marionette click/element waits; in-app uses the available click/locator API. Tool overhead and different browser engines/user agents remain.
No shuffled browser-order repetitions or confidence intervals. Dynamic responses, network routes and origin/CDN variation remain; this is an end-user reference, not a pure CPU/runtime ratio.
Firefox implicit element waits may overrun their configured timeout when its renderer is busy; actual measured elapsed times are preserved.

trials.note: Failure occurred while returning to the local launcher, before another target click. The third requested trial was not started.

excluded_prototypes: Earlier controller revisions could accept an old launcher document, misclassify transient empty script results, or wait for optional timing after content readiness. They are excluded from the primary table.
The retained controller waits for a unique new launcher marker and uses browser-owned implicit element waits, with no high-frequency sandbox creation.

other_observations.earlier_tls_error: PR_END_OF_FILE_ERROR observed on GitHub in an intermediate run; no certificate or TLS check was bypassed.
other_observations.old_browser_exit: After Bilibili, the pre-fix browser logged descriptor allocation failure and mozalloc_abort; subsequent repeated loads stopped. The exact peak object count of that browser run was not captured, so the object quota is independently proven rather than asserted as the sole cause.

old_diagnostic_counter.scope: Mixed loopback/live-diagnostic session, not a timed complex-page sample; cannot be converted into whole-process CPU percentages.

fixes.vulkan_objects: O(1) owner-thread lifetime count replaces per-call Weak<Object> scans; retained command/descriptor dependencies stay counted until final drop. Host-managed mode has no extra 16,384-object quota; bounded sessions retain it.
fixes.shared_anonymous: Existing immutable SharedPage allocation and version/check contract opts into versioned snapshot preparation. No ordinary-byte ordering, permission, ownership, quiescence, quota or storage policy is changed.

shared_anonymous.hardware_mapping_generation: stable for unrelated notifications and direct data writes; software/hardware snapshot modes tested

native_descriptor_objects.before: Host-managed real native allocation fails on batch 4, despite legal driver capacity.
native_descriptor_objects.pool_layout_lifetime: released; driver teardown reports zero GPU bytes
native_descriptor_objects.scope: Mechanism regression, not a browser speedup benchmark.

validation.benchmark_script: compiled and exercised end-to-end; failures kept as failures
validation.reused: Unchanged network/graphics artifact acceptance from previous validation.

privacy: Only aggregate timings, public target URLs, error categories and hashes are published. Guest profiles, raw HTTP logs/cookies, host addresses and traces remain local.

forkserver_dns_follow_up.metric: same host click-command start to target DOM marker; fresh Firefox process per site, one excluded warmup, three requested trials; 1920x792 CSS pixels, 12 CPU slots, host-managed memory, default graphics/security/process prefs

mechanisms.blocked_recvmsg: restore all six saved syscall arguments and syscall number on worker checkpoint; do not reinterpret owner-side -EAGAIN as a new FD; original OFD/poll ownership and already-retired PC are preserved
mechanisms.typed_dns: forward IN RR queries through host resolver on existing workers, retain getaddrinfo for A/AAAA, echo valid questions on errors, keep local names local, preserve complete compressed RR bytes or request TCP retry, normalize stripped additional-record counts

limits: Different engines, caches and network/CDN responses remain uncontrolled; prior in-app results are a reference only.
DOM attachment is not pixel presentation, full resource loading or usable-page latency.
No whole-browser speedup is inferred from resolver microprobes or a small changing sample.

A mixed-site stress run still timed out in Bilibili automation and emitted WebGL context loss / script timeouts; it used the build before the final EDNS count normalization and is retained separately.

mixed_site_stress.completion: aborted on target-element RPC timeout during Bilibili trial 1

coherent_copy_follow_up.method: same host click-command start to target DOM marker; fresh Firefox process per site, one excluded warmup, three requested trials; 1920x792 CSS pixels, 12 CPU slots, host-managed memory, default graphics/security/process prefs

before_profile.scope: 2-second post-Bilibili session-setup sample, before the subsequent recorded navigation; counts are not whole-process CPU percentages

after_profile.scope: 2-second post-Bilibili sample, after retained timing, before the follow-up transition; different sample phase, no controlled CPU-percentage comparison

separate_loopback_transition_ms.metric: Navigate command start to unique launcher DOM marker in separately instrumented post-Bilibili runs; initial session-creation wait is excluded

validation.real_moltenvk_resources: 256 GPU results, descriptor and image operations correct; budget released
validation.unchanged_results_reused: network 67 / kernel 215 per OS; HVF 47 + Mac pressure 1

limits: Different engines, caches and network/CDN responses remain uncontrolled; prior in-app results are a reference only.
DOM attachment is not pixel presentation, full resource loading or usable-page latency.
No whole-browser speedup is inferred from resolver microprobes or a small changing sample.
Consecutive ordered runs, three retained observations per site, evolving HTTP/CDN caches and content; observed median reductions are not a general browser speedup guarantee.
The older in-app medians are a reference, not a fresh same-time or same-engine CPU comparison.
Bilibili still emitted third-party script/chunk-loading errors; content markers do not prove all scripts/resources or video playback work.
Ordinary coherent copies use up to two bounded 4 KiB stack buffers. Entire mapped ranges are still scanned; native zero-copy GPU import is not implemented by this change.
